name: Katherine Bidegaray
description: Concurred, argued that the District Court violated the father's constitutional right to counsel and failed to comply with mandatory notice provisions, thus reversing the termination of parental rights.

name: James Jeremiah Shea
description: Concurred, argued that suspending the portion of the mandatory fine a defendant cannot pay legally imposes the fine, harmonizing statutes and preventing excessive fines.

name: Jim Rice
description: Concurred, argued that overturning Gibbons' holding on the facial unconstitutionality of the mandatory minimum fine corrects a significant error.

name: Katherine M. Bidegaray
description: Dissented, argued that the mandatory minimum fine is facially unconstitutional at the moment of imposition, and suspension does not cure this defect, criticizing the majority's statutory interpretation and disregard for stare decisis.

name: Ingrid Gustafson
description: Dissented with Justice Katherine M. Bidegaray's opinion.

name: Laurie McKinnon
description: Dissented with Justice Katherine M. Bidegaray's opinion.

name: LAURIE MCKINNON
description: Concurred, arguing that the State Policies likely result in unequal treatment and discrimination based on sex, violating the Montana Constitution's equal protection clause, and that the District Court did not abuse its discretion in granting a preliminary injunction.

name: BETH BAKER
description: Concurred narrowly, arguing that the preliminary injunction should be upheld to preserve the status quo, and that the State cannot constitutionally deny citizens the opportunity to obtain identification documents that accurately depict their identity, infringing on individual dignity and privacy.

name: JIM RICE
description: Dissented, arguing that the Court's analysis forces the State to issue falsified legal documents by conflating biological sex with gender identity, and that the State Policies do not discriminate as they treat all persons equally based on biological sex.

name: CORY J. SWANSON
description: Dissented, joining Justice Rice's dissent and arguing that the Court engaged in judicial law-making by intruding on the legislative and executive branches' authority, and that the plaintiffs failed to demonstrate standing or entitlement to a preliminary injunction against the MVD policy.

name: Katherine M. Bidegaray
description: Concurred, argued that BI-8 is a single constitutional amendment and the Attorney General lacked authority to append a fiscal statement.

name: Jim Rice
description: Dissented, argued that BI-8's restriction on government influence or use of resources is a separate constitutional change requiring a separate vote.

name: Cory J. Swanson
description: Dissented, argued that BI-8 impermissibly amends judicial power and litigants' constitutional rights by imposing inflexible deadlines for resolving legal challenges, thus containing multiple unrelated amendments.

name: Chief Justice Cory J. Swanson
description: Concurred, argued that the Commission's due process violations necessitated dismissal, despite finding Knudsen violated professional conduct rules.

name: District Court Judge Jessica T. Fehr
District Court Judge Gregory L. Bonilla
District Court Judge Paul Sullivan
description: Concurred, argued that dismissal was warranted due to extraordinary circumstances and procedural deficiencies, without needing to reach the substantive question of discipline.

name: Justice Katherine M. Bidegaray
description: Dissented, argued that Knudsen's proven misconduct warranted discipline and that the Commission's procedural errors did not justify dismissing the complaint.

name: Jim Rice
description: Concurred, argued that the mandatory minimum custodial sentence for felony DUI is constitutional and not disproportionate to the crime, distinguishing it from mandatory fines.

name: Beth Baker
description: Concurred, argued that the MLUPA's public participation provisions are not facially unconstitutional as the Legislature provided a detailed process for notice and participation, and MAID failed to show the law violates equal protection or that the private covenant issue was justiciable.

name: Justice James Jeremiah Shea
description: Concurred, argued that the Attorney General's revised statement was misleading and did not fairly state what was proposed, and that MNC's proposed statement was compliant.

name: Chief Justice Cory J. Swanson
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that both the Attorney General's and MNC's ballot statements were inadequate and should be remanded for revision.

name: Justice Jim Rice
description: Dissented, argued that the Attorney General's revised statement was legally adequate and should have been upheld, and that MNC's proposed statement was legally inadequate.

name: Beth Baker
description: Concurred, arguing that a rational juror could determine Doman's activity interfered with the traffic stop and obstructed officers' duties, and his constitutional challenges were not properly preserved for appeal.

name: JAMES JEREMIAH SHEA
description: Concurred, highlighting Officer Minaglia's professionalism in handling the encounter, noting that the right to film was not disputed, but Doman's failure to preserve constitutional arguments meant the case was solely about sufficiency of evidence for obstruction.

name: Beth Baker
description: Concurred, argued that the District Court correctly dismissed Netzer's constitutional claims and upheld the constitutionality of HB 702, including both Subsection (1) and Subsection (4), under the Montana Constitution's single-subject and clear-title requirements.

name: JAMES JEREMIAH SHEA
description: Concurred, argued that the District Court did not rely on clearly erroneous findings of fact when it denied Herzog's motion to suppress, and the denial is affirmed.

name: KATHERINE M BIDEGARAY
description: Concurred, argued that while the totality of circumstances justified the investigatory stop, courts must be cautious not to broadly interpret innocuous conduct as grounds for particularized suspicion, to avoid diluting constitutional protections against unreasonable governmental intrusion.

name: LAURIE MCKINNON
description: Concurred with the concurring opinion of Justice Katherine Bidegaray.

name: INGRID GUSTAFSON
description: Concurred with the concurring opinion of Justice Katherine Bidegaray.

name: Justice Laurie McKinnon
description: Concurred, argued that establishing a presumption for attorney's fees is essential for government transparency and criticized the dissents for unprofessional attacks on the Court's integrity.

name: Justice James Jeremiah Shea
description: Concurred, argued that providing guidance for discretionary attorney fee awards is well-precedented and necessary to ensure citizens can enforce their constitutional right to know.

name: Justice Katherine M. Bidegaray
description: Concurred, argued that providing guidance for discretionary attorney fee awards is well-precedented and necessary to ensure citizens can enforce their constitutional right to know.

name: Justice Ingrid Gustafson
description: Concurred, argued that providing guidance for discretionary attorney fee awards is well-precedented and necessary to ensure citizens can enforce their constitutional right to know.

name: Justice Beth Baker
description: Dissented, argued that attorney's fees are discretionary, the District Court did not abuse its discretion, and the majority's new presumption is overly simplistic and departs from precedent.

name: Chief Justice Cory J. Swanson
description: Dissented, argued that the District Court's decision was correct, the majority's ruling lacked legal basis and departed from precedent, and emphasized the Chief Justice's duty to interpret the law and Constitution.

name: Justice Jim Rice
description: Dissented, argued that the majority opinion lacked governing law, set aside longstanding principles, and was driven by personal preferences, undermining the Court's legitimacy.

name: BETH BAKER
description: Concurred, argued that DEQ adequately analyzed noise impacts but failed to take a "hard look" at lighting impacts and greenhouse gas emissions, requiring further MEPA analysis, but the permit vacatur was reversed due to lack of specific findings.

name: Justice Jim Rice
description: Concurred, argued that the vacatur of the permit should be reversed because the case is moot under the particular circumstances, as the facility is already operational and DEQ's decision not to conduct GHG analysis was an informed discretionary determination at the time.

name: Justice Dirk Sandefur
description: Concurred, argued that the vacatur of the permit should be reversed because the case is moot under the particular circumstances, as the facility is already operational and DEQ's decision not to conduct GHG analysis was an informed discretionary determination at the time.

name: Justice Laurie McKinnon
description: Dissented, argued that the Court undermines MEPA's significance in protecting Montanans' constitutional right to a clean environment by reversing the permit vacatur without providing an effective remedy for the clear MEPA violations regarding GHG emissions.

name: Justice Ingrid Gustafson
description: Dissented, argued that the Court undermines MEPA's significance in protecting Montanans' constitutional right to a clean environment by reversing the permit vacatur without providing an effective remedy for the clear MEPA violations regarding GHG emissions.

name: Jim Rice
description: Concurred, argued that the Department of Natural Resources and Conservation (DNRC) correctly interpreted the Montana Water Use Act (MWUA) by categorizing mine dewatering, when not used beneficially, as neither a beneficial use nor waste, thus falling outside the MWUA's permitting process, and that this interpretation does not render the Act unconstitutional.

name: Mike McGrath
description: Concurred with the majority opinion and argued that Tintina could not raise the Appellants' standing for the first time on appeal, but that Appellants do have standing to challenge DNRC's permitting decision based on their recreational and aesthetic interests.

name: Laurie McKinnon
description: Dissented, argued that mine dewatering should be considered a beneficial use requiring a water use permit under the MWUA, that the Court's interpretation creates an unconstitutional loophole, and that the DNRC's policy is inconsistent with statutory language and legislative intent to protect Montana's water resources.

name: Ingrid Gustafson
description: Dissented, joined in the dissenting opinion of Justice Laurie McKinnon.

name: MIKE MCGRATH
description: Concurred, argued that the District Court erred in finding the statute unconstitutional, as the State can explicitly prohibit local government units from exercising certain powers under the Montana Constitution, which extends to local initiative powers.

name: Laurie McKinnon
description: Dissented, argued that the people's constitutional right to initiative is fundamental and should not be limited by legislative statutes beyond the explicit constitutional constraints, making the statute unconstitutional.

name: Ingrid Gustafson
description: Dissented, argued that the State's claim that statutes can restrict the constitutional right of initiative is absurd and undermines constitutional supremacy, joining Justice McKinnon's dissent.

name: James Jeremiah Shea
description: Concurred, argued that a gubernatorial privilege exists under Montana law, rooted in the 1889 and 1972 Constitutions, to ensure candid advice for the Governor's constitutional duties, but it is subject to in camera review and strict parameters.

name: Laurie McKinnon
description: Dissented, argued that no executive or gubernatorial privilege should be recognized under Montana law, as the Constitution's plain language and the right to know already provide a framework for government functions without needing a formalized privilege, and recognizing such a privilege infringes on public transparency.

name: Ingrid Gustafson
description: Dissented, argued that no executive or gubernatorial privilege should be recognized under Montana law, as the Constitution's plain language and the right to know already provide a framework for government functions without needing a formalized privilege, and recognizing such a privilege infringes on public transparency.

name: Leslie Halligan
description: Dissented, argued that no executive or gubernatorial privilege should be recognized under Montana law, as the Constitution's plain language and the right to know already provide a framework for government functions without needing a formalized privilege, and recognizing such a privilege infringes on public transparency.

name: Beth Baker
description: Concurred, argued that the challenged laws violate Montana's constitutional rights to privacy, equal protection, and free speech by infringing on personal and procreative autonomy without a compelling, medically acknowledged health risk.

name: Jim Rice
description: Dissented, argued that the court's absolutist application of the right to privacy fails to account for the State's vital role in protecting human life, that the constitutional history does not support an abortion right, and that the challenged laws should not be dismissed as entirely unconstitutional.

name: Justice Beth Baker
description: Concurred, argued that the District Court correctly granted a preliminary injunction based on the plaintiffs' fundamental right to privacy.

name: LAURIE MCKINNON
description: Concurred, argued that the equal protection claim should also be addressed, stating that discrimination based on transgender status is sex discrimination and a suspect class, triggering strict scrutiny.

name: INGRID GUSTAFSON
description: Concurred with Justice Laurie McKinnon's separate opinion.

name: Justice Jim Rice
description: Concurred in part with upholding the injunction on medical restrictions but dissented from enjoining the funding prohibition, arguing funding decisions should be subject to rational basis review.

name: Justice Ingrid Gustafson
description: Concurred, argued that the District Court did not abuse its discretion in granting the preliminary injunction because the challenged provisions likely violate the Montana Constitution's right to privacy and equal protection.

name: Justice Laurie McKinnon
description: Concurred, argued that the Court's decision was correct in affirming the preliminary injunction and that the equal protection claim was properly addressed, emphasizing the judiciary's role in upholding the Constitution against legislative overreach.

name: Justice Beth Baker
description: Concurred, argued that the District Court correctly applied strict scrutiny to the privacy claims, but that the Court should have exercised judicial restraint by not addressing the equal protection issues at the preliminary injunction stage.

name: Justice James Jeremiah Shea
description: Concurred with Justice Beth Baker's special concurring opinion.

name: Justice Jim Rice
description: Dissented, argued that the challenged bills concern government healthcare funding, not restrictions on medical procedures, and should be assessed under rational basis review, not strict scrutiny, and that the District Court failed to apply the presumption of constitutionality.

name: Ingrid Gustafson
description: Concurred, argued that the District Court did not abuse its discretion by granting a preliminary injunction against HB 575 and HB 721, as both bills infringe on the fundamental right to privacy and access to abortion care under the Montana Constitution.

name: Jim Rice
description: Concurred that the preliminary injunction for HB 721 was properly granted, but dissented regarding HB 575, arguing that HB 575 serves a legitimate state interest in ensuring pre-viability abortions and should be presumed constitutional.

name: MIKE MCGRATH
description: Concurred, argued that the Secretary's fees for the voter file are lawful and do not conflict with the NVRA, and that the 'right to know' was not violated due to the lack of specificity in ACORN's request.

name: MIKE MCGRATH, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the warrantless entry was justified under the community caretaker doctrine due to exigent circumstances and that no Brady violation occurred.

name: Justice Laurie McKinnon
description: Dissented, argued that the Court's analysis was confusing, misapprehended Caniglia, and improperly extended the community caretaker doctrine to home entries without sufficient probable cause or exigent circumstances.

name: Justice Ingrid Gustafson
description: Dissented, argued that the Court's analysis was confusing, misapprehended Caniglia, and improperly extended the community caretaker doctrine to home entries without sufficient probable cause or exigent circumstances.

name: Justice Dirk Sandefur
description: Dissented, argued that the Court's analysis was confusing, misapprehended Caniglia, and improperly extended the community caretaker doctrine to home entries without sufficient probable cause or exigent circumstances.

name: Laurie McKinnon
description: Concurred, argued that the Parental Consent for Abortion Act of 2013 violates a minor's fundamental right to privacy and equal protection under the Montana Constitution.

name: Jim Rice
description: Concurred with the ultimate holdings but disagreed with the equal protection analysis and criticized the judiciary's delay in resolving the case.

name: Mike McGrath
description: Concurred, argued that the Montana Constitution's right to a clean and healthful environment includes a stable climate system and that the MEPA Limitation unconstitutionally infringes upon this right, and affirmed the District Court's denial of psychiatric examinations.

name: Dirk Sandefur
description: Concurred, argued that the right to a clean and healthful environment includes a stable climate system and that the MEPA review limitations are unconstitutional, but questioned the lack of particularized causation evidence and the global nature of the problem, while agreeing plaintiffs had minimally sufficient standing.

name: Jim Rice
description: Dissented, argued that the plaintiffs lacked standing because their alleged injury was abstract and indistinguishable from the general public, and that the MEPA Limitation was not shown to directly cause their alleged harm, thus judicial relief would not redress it.

name: Chief Justice Mike McGrath
description: Concurred, argued that the Attorney General erred in concluding the ballot issue was legally insufficient because its components (political party nominations, specification of offices, signature-gathering limitation, and legislative authority) are closely related and do not violate the separate-vote requirement.

name: Mike McGrath, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the District Court abused its discretion by denying attorney fees under the private attorney general doctrine, as the Legislature acted in bad faith by passing an unconstitutional bill with willful disregard for constitutional obligations, and the Appellants vindicated important constitutional interests.

name: Justice Jim Rice
description: Dissented, argued that the Court's reasoning for applying the private attorney general doctrine lacks merit under precedent, and the District Court did not abuse its discretion by denying fees, as the case was a 'garden variety' constitutional challenge not deserving of attorney fees.

name: Justice Dirk Sandefur
description: Dissented, argued that he joins in the dissenting opinion of Justice Rice.

name: Justice Ingrid Gustafson
description: Concurred, argued that the District Court correctly found the plaintiffs had standing and that HB 349, HB 112, and § 2 of SB 319 were unconstitutional infringements on the Board of Regents' authority. She dissented on attorney fees, arguing they should have been awarded due to the vindication of important constitutional interests and the State's concessions.

name: Justice Laurie McKinnon
description: Concurred with the majority opinion on the unconstitutionality of the bills and standing. She dissented on attorney fees, arguing they should have been awarded.

name: Chief Justice Mike McGrath
description: Concurred with the majority opinion on the unconstitutionality of the bills and standing. He concurred on attorney fees, arguing the District Court did not abuse its discretion in denying them as equitable factors were not met and legislative bad faith was not clearly established.

name: Justice Beth Baker
description: Concurred with the majority opinion on the unconstitutionality of the bills and standing, and agreed with Chief Justice McGrath's opinion on attorney fees.

name: Justice James Jeremiah Shea
description: Concurred with the majority opinion on the unconstitutionality of the bills and standing. He concurred on attorney fees, agreeing that the necessity for private enforcement was not sufficiently demonstrated.

name: Justice Jim Rice
description: Dissented, argued that the plaintiffs lacked standing to challenge the legislation because the Board of Regents holds exclusive constitutional authority over the university system, not members of the university community.

name: Justice Dirk M. Sandefur
description: Dissented, concurred with Justice Rice that the plaintiffs lacked standing. However, he stated that if standing were found, he would concur that the challenged legislation unconstitutionally infringed on the Board of Regents' authority.

name: LAURIE MCKINNON JUDGE
description: Concurred, argued that the mandatory minimum fine statute is facially unconstitutional because it prevents courts from considering proportionality factors like ability to pay, violating the right against excessive fines.

name: Justice James Jeremiah Shea
description: Dissented, argued that the mandatory fine statute could be harmonized with the general sentencing statute to allow for ability-to-pay considerations without declaring it unconstitutional.

name: Justice Jim Rice
description: Dissented, argued that the mandatory fine statute is constitutional, distinguishable from prior invalidated statutes, and the Court's decision unnecessarily overturns precedent and is overbroad.

name: Justice Beth Baker
description: Dissented, joined Justice Rice's dissenting opinion.

name: Ingrid Gustafson
description: Concurred, delivered the opinion of the court, finding the Attorney General's ballot statement deficient and certifying a new one.

name: MIKE MCGRATH CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the District Court abused its discretion by denying attorney fees under the private attorney general doctrine, as the Appellants vindicated important constitutional rights against an unconstitutional bill passed with willful disregard for legislative rules.

name: Justice Jim Rice
description: Dissented, argued that the District Court did not abuse its discretion in denying fees, as the private attorney general doctrine should be invoked sparingly and the majority's reasoning lacks merit.

name: Dirk Sandefur
description: Dissented, argued that the District Court did not abuse its discretion in denying fees, as the private attorney general doctrine should be invoked sparingly and the majority's reasoning lacks merit.

name: MIKE McGRATH
description: Concurred, argued that the four challenged election laws unconstitutionally interfered with or burdened the fundamental right to vote, requiring strict or middle-tier scrutiny which the State failed to satisfy.

name: LAURIE McKINNON
description: Concurred, argued that HB 506 impermissibly interfered with the right to vote and should be subject to strict scrutiny, not middle-tier scrutiny.

name: INGRID GUSTAFSON
description: Concurred, argued that HB 506 impermissibly interfered with the right to vote and should be subject to strict scrutiny, not middle-tier scrutiny.

name: Beth Baker
description: Concurred in part, dissented in part, argued that HB 506 imposed only a minimal burden on voting rights and was a reasonable regulation, thus should not be disturbed.

name: DIRK M. SANDEFUR
description: Concurred in part, dissented in part, argued that HB 506 was unconstitutional but that HB 176, HB 530, and SB 169 were not facially unconstitutional, as the Court's analysis was based on erroneous legal standards and findings of fact.

name: JIM RICE
description: Concurred in part, dissented in part, argued that HB 176, HB 530, and SB 169 were not facially unconstitutional, as the Court's analysis was based on erroneous legal standards and findings of fact.

name: Jim Rice Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Attorney General correctly determined that Ballot Initiative #2 violated the separate-vote requirement by proposing multiple, unrelated constitutional changes as a single amendment, which would prevent voters from expressing their opinions on each proposed change separately.

name: Ingrid Gustafson
description: Concurred, argued that the school districts' mask policies did not implicate fundamental rights under the Montana Constitution and were rationally related to the legitimate government interest of stemming the spread of COVID-19.

name: Justice Laurie McKinnon
description: Concurred, argued that the amended SVORA is punitive and cannot be retroactively applied, violating the ex post facto clause.

name: DIRK M. SANDEFUR
description: Concurred, argued that the amended SVORA is punitive and cannot be retroactively applied, violating the ex post facto clause, and would overrule State v. Mount.

name: INGRID GUSTAFSON
description: Concurred, argued that the amended SVORA is punitive and cannot be retroactively applied, and would overrule parts of Mount and Wagner.

name: Chief Justice Mike McGrath
description: Concurred, argued that SVORA is unconstitutional under Article II, Section 28(2) regarding restoration of rights, and would overrule Mount.

name: Justice Jim Rice
description: Dissented, argued that the SVORA statute is constitutional and should be upheld, consistent with prior precedent.

name: DIRK SANDEFUR
description: Concurred, arguing that the traffic stop was unlawfully prolonged beyond its initial justification without sufficient particularized suspicion for a drug investigation, thus violating constitutional protections against unreasonable searches and seizures.

name: LAURIE MCKINNON JUDGE
description: Concurred, argued that the State failed to demonstrate a medically acknowledged, bona fide health risk justifying the restriction on APRNs providing abortion care, thus infringing on a woman's fundamental right to privacy to choose her healthcare provider.

name: Ingrid Gustafson
description: Concurred, arguing that the statute unconstitutionally violates the right to equal protection of the law for parents and children subject to dependent-neglect proceedings under ICWA by denying them prompt emergency protective services hearings.

name: BETH BAKER
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court did not violate Staudenmayer's confrontation right by admitting minute entries and did not abuse its discretion by denying the motion to continue.

name: Justice Laurie McKinnon
description: Dissented, argued that the minute entries were testimonial hearsay and their admission violated Staudenmayer's confrontation right, requiring a new trial.

name: Justice James Jeremiah Shea
description: Dissented, argued that the trial court abused its discretion by denying the motion to continue, which prejudiced the defendant's substantial rights.

name: Justice Ingrid Gustafson
description: Dissented, joined the dissenting opinions of Justice McKinnon and Justice Shea.

name: Laurie McKinnon
description: Concurred, argued that the group home manager was a private party, not a state actor, and Larson consented to the confiscation of his electronic devices by agreeing to the group home rules.

name: Justice Beth Baker
description: Concurred, arguing that the warrantless search of Mefford's phone exceeded the scope of his consent and was not justified by the probation search exception, thus violating constitutional rights.

name: Justice James Jeremiah Shea
description: Dissented, arguing that while the search exceeded consent, it was a permissible probation search based on reasonable suspicion from the totality of circumstances, and the evidence should not be suppressed.

name: Chief Justice Mike McGrath
description: Dissented, joining Justice Shea's opinion that the search was a permissible probation search.

name: Justice Jim Rice
description: Dissented, joining Justice Shea's opinion that the search was a permissible probation search.

name: Chief Justice Mike McGrath
description: Concurred, argued that the proposed legislative referendum HB 325 is facially unconstitutional and ripe for judicial resolution based on binding prior precedent.

name: Justice Beth Baker
description: Dissented, argued that the issues were not ripe for review due to a lack of immediate temporal urgency and that the court should not address the merits of the constitutional challenge.

name: Justice Jim Rice
description: Dissented, argued that the issues were not ripe for review and joined Justice Baker's dissenting opinion.

name: MIKE MCGRATH
description: Concurred, argued that the Attorney General wrongly applied an appropriation restriction to a constitutional amendment initiative.

name: JIM RICE
description: Concurred, affirming the District Court's decision on all three issues, finding no equal protection violation in the Batson challenge, no plain error in the prosecutor's closing remarks, and that the prior conviction was constitutionally valid for enhancement.

name: BETH BAKER
description: Concurred, but argued that Montana's Batson framework should be revisited to provide greater protection against discriminatory peremptory challenges, acknowledging its failure to address implicit bias and its impact on racial equality in jury selection.

name: Justice Beth Baker
description: Concurred, argued that the facial challenge to HB 286 was ripe but failed on its merits because the statute's plain language does not establish a presumption against State ownership or deprive Advocates of a constitutionally protected interest, and the denial of the motion to amend was not an abuse of discretion as the proposed amendment would not present a definite, concrete injury.

name: Chief Justice Mike McGrath
description: Concurred, argued that the private gathering of committee members, lacking a quorum, was not a formal public meeting subject to open meeting laws or the constitutional right to public access, distinguishing it from previous cases involving more formally structured bodies.

name: Justice Laurie McKinnon
description: Dissented, argued that the Court's decision creates a judicial exception to the public's constitutional right to know, undermines the intent for open government, and that purposefully excluding members to avoid a quorum violates the constitutional right to know.

name: Dirk Sandefur
description: Concurred, argued that the warrantless search was lawful under the probation search exception and the exclusionary rule did not apply to the manner of entry or detention.

name: Beth Baker
description: Concurred, argued that while troubled by the officers' treatment of Peoples, affirming the decision was necessary due to precedent on the exclusionary rule.

name: Ingrid Gustafson
description: Dissented, argued that Peoples's constitutional rights were violated by the unreasonable search and the evidence should have been suppressed.

name: Laurie McKinnon
description: Dissented, argued that Peoples's constitutional rights were violated by the unreasonable search and the evidence should have been suppressed.

name: JIM RICE, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the ruling is narrowly required by Lange and that the officer was initially justified in following the suspect onto the driveway, but further investigation required a warrant once privacy was asserted and residency confirmed.

name: Justice Beth Baker
description: Concurred, argued that the subpoenas were impermissibly overbroad, exceeded legislative authority, and sought confidential information not related to a valid legislative purpose, thus violating separation of powers and privacy rights.

name: DIRK M. SANDEFUR
description: Concurred, argued that the subpoenas were invalid based on the constitutional doctrine of separation of powers, which limits legislative power and protects the judiciary's independence.

name: Justice Laurie McKinnon
description: Concurred, argued that quashing the subpoenas was mandated by the constitutional doctrine of separation of powers, as the Legislature was investigating purported judicial misconduct, which is not a valid legislative purpose and interferes with a co-equal branch.

name: Dirk Sandefur
description: Concurred, argued that Staker had a subjective expectation of privacy but it was not objectively reasonable in society, thus no constitutional search occurred.

name: Justice James Jeremiah Shea
description: Concurred, arguing that SB 140 is constitutional as it aligns with the Framers' intent for judicial selection, which did not mandate a commission and allowed legislative discretion, and that the new process provides sufficient vetting.

name: JIM RICE, J.
description: Concurred, but wrote separately to address the extraordinary and extraconstitutional actions taken by the Legislature and Department of Justice during the proceeding, which he viewed as contemptuous and destructive to the democratic system.

name: Justice Laurie McKinnon
description: Dissented, arguing that SB 140 is unconstitutional because it fails to provide a merit-based selection process for judicial nominees as intended by the Framers, thereby allowing direct gubernatorial appointments and threatening judicial independence.

name: Justice Beth Baker
description: Concurred, argued that the District Court's errors in admitting the forensic interview were harmless and that the GPS monitoring statute is facially constitutional.

name: Laurie McKinnon
description: Concurred, delivering the majority opinion that affirmed the defendant's convictions, finding the Privacy in Communications statute constitutional and correctly applied.

name: Justice Dirk Sandefur
description: Concurred, argued that "legal demands" in MWUA do not include MWQA nondegradation standards and that MWUA's objection limitations do not violate constitutional environmental rights, as other statutes provide adequate remedies.

name: Justice Laurie McKinnon
description: Dissented, argued that "legal demands" under MWUA should include MWQA nondegradation standards, and that the DNRC should consider dewatering effects on Outstanding Resource Waters (ORWs) as part of "legal availability" to protect constitutional environmental rights.

name: Justice Ingrid Gustafson
description: Dissented, joining Justice McKinnon's opinion that "legal demands" under MWUA should include MWQA nondegradation standards and that the DNRC should consider dewatering effects on ORWs.

name: Justice Ingrid Gustafson
description: Concurred, argued that the District Court erred by not considering rehabilitation evidence when determining if Keefe was irreparably corrupt, violating his due process rights, and remanded for a new sentencing hearing.

name: Chief Justice Mike McGrath
description: Concurred in reversing the resentencing but dissented from remanding for another sentencing, arguing that Montana's Constitution warrants stronger protection for youthful defendants and that life without parole for juveniles should be presumed unconstitutional unless proven otherwise. He would have struck the "without parole" provision.

name: Justice Dirk Sandefur
description: Concurred that the District Court erred in not considering rehabilitation evidence and that Keefe had no right to his own expert or a jury determination on incorrigibility. He dissented from remanding for resentencing, arguing the State failed to prove Keefe was irreparably corrupt and would have simply struck the parole eligibility restriction.

name: Justice Laurie McKinnon
description: Concurred on the expert appointment and jury determination issues but dissented on the sufficiency of evidence, arguing that Keefe received an individualized resentencing where youth characteristics were considered and the sentence was not disproportionate.

name: Justice Jim Rice
description: Concurred and dissented with Justice McKinnon's opinion.
